title: Attributes: The Extra Spice 🌶️
description: Learn common attributes like id, class, title, and how to use them.

slides.title: Why Attributes? 🧂
slides.content:
# Adding Extra Meaning & Functionality

Attributes give elements special powers:
- They identify elements (`id`, `class`).
- They provide interactive hints (`title`, `placeholder`).
- They change behaviour (`href`, `src`, `disabled`).

Every attribute has a **name** and a **value** written as `name="value"`. The value is always wrapped in quotes (single or double, but double is standard).

slides.title: The `id` Attribute 🆔
slides.content:
# A Unique Name for One Element `id` gives an element a **unique** identifier. No two elements on the same page should share the same `id`. ```html

Welcome

``` - Used for CSS styling (`#main-heading { ... }`). - Used for JavaScript to grab that specific element. - Used for anchor links (`Go to top`). Think of `id` like a social security number – one per person!

quizData.question: You can give the same id to two different paragraphs.
quizData.explanation: Ids must be unique. Duplicate ids break HTML validity and cause JavaScript/CSS conflicts.

slides.title: The `class` Attribute 🏷️
slides.content:
# Grouping Elements Together `class` can be shared among multiple elements. It's perfect for styling groups. ```html

Important note

Another important note

``` - An element can have **several classes**: `class="highlight bold-text"` (separated by space). - Use classes as your main styling hook in CSS. Id is unique; class is like a team jersey – many players can wear it.

quizData.question: How do you assign multiple classes to one element?
quizData.explanation: Separate class names with a space inside the same attribute value.

slides.title: The `title` Attribute 💬
slides.content:
# Tooltips on Hover `title` displays extra information when the user hovers over the element. ```html

Hover over me!

``` - Often used on links, images, or abbreviations. - Not a replacement for vital information – screen readers may not announce it consistently. - Keep it short and helpful.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Double Quotes Are Standard

Although single quotes work, using `="..."` is the widely accepted convention. Pick one style and stick with it throughout your project.
